evidence.domain_coverage_summary: All 11 predeclared functional domains have a canonical, officially-recognized, currently-maintained third-party (or first-party-adjacent, e.g. Django) library available on PyPI. No domain returned a gap. Coverage is treated as near-total (98/100) rather than a perfect 100 to acknowledge that this is a bounded sample of domains, not an exhaustive enumeration of every conceivable software domain, per the predeclared-sampling caveat that raw popularity/coverage indicators are declared evidence with stated limitations rather than an absolute proof of universal coverage.

evidence.maintenance_activity_summary: Every sampled package across the frozen domain list shows releases or changelog entries within the 2026 calendar year, several within the last one to two months of the snapshot date, and most track new CPython release readiness within the same release cycle (3.14 classifiers already present for numpy, pandas, requests, cryptography, boto3, pytest, fastapi, aiohttp, pydantic per the pyreadiness.org cross-check). This indicates a highly active, well-maintained package ecosystem across sampled domains, supporting a high but not maximal normalized score (97/100) to leave room for packages/domains outside the sampled set that may show slower cadence.

evidence.methodology_note: Predeclared sampling per ecosystem.md Section 'Predeclared sampling'. Domains and target packages were frozen before evidence collection using a language-neutral selection rule, not first-search-result or alphabetical accident. Raw popularity indicators (downloads, stars) are used only as declared supporting evidence, never as a standalone proxy, and are reported with their limitations.
evidence.retrieval_route: Web search snapshot via provider-brokered search tool, single retrieval route applied uniformly (PyPI project pages, PyPI JSON API mirrors, pypistats.org, deps.dev, releasealert.dev, pyreadiness.org, and package changelog/readthedocs pages). Same route and examination depth (project page + latest release metadata + changelog) applied per sampled package.
evidence.selection_rule: For each functional domain, the target library is the single most-downloaded PyPI package that (a) is explicitly named as the standard/most common solution for that domain in the domain's own official documentation, canonical tutorial, or the PyPA/Python packaging ecosystem index (e.g. pyreadiness.org's tracked 'most popular Python packages' cross-reference list, which itself derives ranking from PyPI JSON-API + download telemetry), and (b) appears in the hugovk/top-pypi-packages monthly top-15,000-by-downloads snapshot. This rule is identical in structure across languages sharded to other workers: 'externally documented canonical library for the domain, cross-checked against an independent package-index popularity snapshot'.
